cases.question: Find companies that spend between 10% and 20% of their revenue on R&D.
cases.result_summary: count 40 (capped). Top: GOOG (rnd $68.97B on $445.9B rev = ~15.5%), MSFT ($35.6B on $331.8B = ~10.7%), AVGO. All within the 10-20% band. Two-sided ratio of two line items, as intended.
cases.confusion_note: OBVIOUS. The ScreenCondition RELATION form doc + `relation` enum explicitly lists 'ratio_between (min <= A/B <= max ... as a fraction of B)' and bounds are FRACTIONS. Resolving rnd/revenue via find_fsconcept was direct (both curated:true rank-1). No guessing, no trial-error.
cases.reason: Non-empty, each result's R&D/revenue lands in 10-20%; a genuine two-line-item ratio band, not a single-metric threshold.

cases.question: Which companies have capital expenditure of around 8% of revenue?
cases.result_summary: count 40 (capped). Top: XOM (capex_to_revenue 0.0808 = ~8.1%), AMAT, etc. — capital-intensive energy/semis names. Response surfaced a _conventions note explaining capex is stored NEGATIVE (outflow); the server matched by magnitude (capex value -$29.17B) and reported capex_to_revenue positive ~0.08.
cases.confusion_note: OBVIOUS. The `relation` enum + `target`/`band` fields spell out ratio_near verbatim ('capex around 8% of revenue -> metricA=capex, ratio_near, metricB=revenue, target=0.08') — literally the example. find_fsconcept returned capex with is_inverted:true/sign metadata and the guide said the SERVER handles sign, so I did NOT reason about the minus. Server did the right thing (magnitude). Zero guessing.
cases.reason: capex/revenue sits near 8% (XOM 0.0808), capital-intensive names, sign handled by magnitude not literal minus.

cases.question: Find companies whose R&D is at least 15% of their revenue.
cases.result_summary: count 40 (capped). Top: GOOG (rnd $68.97B / rev $445.9B = 15.5%), plus a heavy-R&D name at rnd $8.64B on $18.67B rev (~46%, software/loss-maker). One-sided fraction-of relation R&D/revenue >= 0.15.
cases.confusion_note: OBVIOUS. `relation:'higher_than'` doc gives the exact example 'R&D >= 15% of revenue -> metricA=rnd, higher_than, metricB=revenue, multiple=0.15' and states multiple is a FRACTION. Concepts reused from r1. No trial-error.
cases.reason: R&D-heavy names with R&D/revenue >= 0.15, non-empty and plausible (Alphabet + software/semis).

cases.question: Show me companies where free cash flow covers the dividend at least twice over.
cases.result_summary: count 40 (capped). Top: NVDA (FCF $119.08B), AAPL, etc. — large FCF-generative dividend payers. Coverage relation FCF >= 2x dividends. dividends_paid resolved as curated rank-1 (is_inverted:true; server handles the outflow sign).
cases.confusion_note: OBVIOUS. 'covers the dividend at least twice over' = A >= 2xB -> higher_than with multiple=2 ('cash >= 2x debt -> multiple=2' example in the doc). dividends_paid is stored-negative (is_inverted) but the guide is explicit the SERVER applies sign, so I passed the concept raw and got sensible payers. No guess. (Minor: results skew to mega-cap growth like NVDA whose dividend is tiny — a huge FCF/tiny-div ratio trivially clears 2x; that is correct per the literal request, just not a 'dividend aristocrat' cut. Not a defect.)
cases.reason: Dividend payers with FCF >= 2x dividends paid, non-empty and plausible (coverage relation honored).

cases.question: Find companies with a net profit margin above 20%.
cases.result_summary: count 40 (capped). Top: NVDA (net_margin 0.6297), AAPL (net_income $128.9B on $466.8B rev). matched.kind='level', all above 0.20. Plain single-metric level screen.
cases.confusion_note: OBVIOUS. find_fsconcept returned the `net_margin` ratio (curated, unit:percent). The threshold doc is explicit: a ratio/percent metric is a FRACTION -> send 0.20 for 20%. Used the plain metric+pattern (concept/pattern/threshold) form, NOT the relation form. No guessing.
cases.reason: Control works: single-metric net_margin > 0.20, non-empty, sensible high-margin names.

top_defects: none — all 5 cases were unambiguous from the schema; the ScreenCondition RELATION-form docs give near-verbatim examples for ratio_between / ratio_near / higher_than (multiple as a FRACTION), and the sign/is_inverted metadata is explicitly server-applied so the client never had to reason about capex/dividends being stored negative
